summary: Kaniksu lookout on 7,009-foot Scotchman Peak from 1922; D-6 cupola cabin c.1926; two sources give abandonment in the 1950s; a magazine article says a few boards and rock remain.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s according to two sources; firelookout.com's header says the 1970s. A magazine article says scraps of wood, hardware and part of the lower rock work remain.

visit.trail_note: About three miles of trail with nearly 3,700 feet of elevation gain, according to a magazine article about the climb. The same article says the Forest Service closed the trail in September 2015 and it reopened in 2016.

events.note: Established by the Forest Service; the magazine calls the first setup a 'rag camp', a pup tent near a tree

notes_for_editor: Abandonment: 1950s in the Forest Lookouts page and the magazine article, but firelookout.com's header runs to 1970s; the record's 1950 abandonment event is not supported by the sources read (they say 1950s), so it was left out of events. The magazine article gives no publication date in the text read; it is the only source for the lightning deaths and the remains, so treat both as single-source. The magazine's 'rag camp' wording replaces an earlier 'bare camp' that no source used. Access: the article reports the trail closed in September 2015 and reopened in 2016; it gives no current rules, and the story says none was found. Staffing: only the 1924 Dr. Broady caption is documented; the record's staffing is unknown. The Scotchman Peak Wilderness reference comes from a photo caption, not a rules page. Record kind is 'ground' and material 'wood', consistent with the D-6 cupola cabin described.
